findings.description: Gateway ReceiptMaintenance retains only one ExportLease. A preview in another tab overwrites the first live tab export identity, so its next chunk/rotate rejects archive_expired even though the core now retains both export snapshots. This defeats the implemented independent-tab export behavior.
findings.reproduction: F1 in .work/v240/full1-runtime-reproductions.json: connection A preview, connection B preview, A chunk -> archive_expired.
findings.requestedFix: Use bounded independently owned leases coordinated with core snapshot retention/expiry; disconnect invalidates only that owner. Add a full gateway multi-tab export regression, retaining exact offset/ownership/complete-export rotation checks.
findings.coverageGap: New two-tab test exercises Ledger snapshots only; gateway tests cover one lease, expiry, owner and drain but not simultaneous previews.

findings.description: A definitively rejected stop writes a nextStop cooldown. If turn/completed later finishes the run via the notification path, it deletes nextRead but not nextStop. The run leaves outstanding(), so that cooldown is never visited again; repeated affected runs grow the Map without retention bounds.
findings.reproduction: F2 in .work/v240/full1-runtime-reproductions.json: actual stop not_sent path then completion event leaves cooldown size 1 with zero outstanding runs.
findings.requestedFix: Clear both cooldown maps on all terminal transitions and prune orphan run entries without evicting live/unknown ownership. Cover completion, unknown stop, queued stop/read races and plan/run retention.
findings.coverageGap: Scheduler tests cover rejected-stop throttling but do not assert terminal cooldown reclamation.

findings.description: DiagnosticRedactor does not register HARNESS_PROVIDER_KEY_DEFAULT or HARNESS_PROVIDER_KEY_<32HEX> values, although configFromEnvironment explicitly supports those managed provider variables. A diagnostic/native error containing the configured credential as a bare value survives both text and structured redaction, unlike the legacy HARNESS_PROVIDER_API_KEY path.
findings.reproduction: F3 in .work/v240/full1-runtime-reproductions.json uses synthetic values only and proves both configured variable forms remain in text and structured error output.
findings.requestedFix: Recognize the exact supported managed provider credential variable forms, including assignment/key projections, with regression coverage through runtime/native diagnostic paths. Preserve the separate production launcher credential boundary; do not expose additional secrets to the worker merely for redaction.
findings.coverageGap: Existing redaction tests cover legacy HARNESS_PROVIDER_API_KEY and bearer tokens but not the managed multi-provider variable names.
findings.limitation: This is a proven redaction gap for supported env-provided credentials, not evidence that a real production credential has leaked. Production launcher loads credentials separately and must retain its least-privilege boundary.

findings.description: After awaiting rpc.close() and its owned cleanup proof, the Linux launcher test probes rpc.processId using process.kill(pid, 0). A reused numeric PID can falsely fail an otherwise successful cleanup assertion. This particular call is signal 0 and does not kill an unrelated process.
findings.requestedFix: Assert the captured spawned ChildProcess close/exit plus launcher cleanup proof; do not probe an old numeric PID after owned close. Coordinate with the parent tooling preflight PID-ownership fix.
